runs.text: Article 55 of the Labor Standards Act and Article 30 of its Enforcement Decree

runs: , an employer must give an employee who has worked all of their scheduled working days in a week at least one paid day off per week (the “weekly holiday”). The wage paid for that day is weekly holiday pay (“jujusudang”).

items: Your scheduled weekly working hours must be

. (Strictly this is measured as a 4-week average, but if your hours are the same every week, judging by a single week is fine. If your hours vary a lot week to week, this calculator’s result may not match reality.)

items.text: worked all of your scheduled days

items: that week with no absences. (Being late or leaving early doesn’t matter, but an absence means no pay for that week.)

runs: “Scheduled hours” means the hours set in your labor contract, not the hours you actually worked more or less. Even if your contract is for more than 40 hours a week, only up to 8 hours (the maximum) counts toward this calculation.

This is a reference-only mock calculation. This English page is a translation of the original Korean tool; actual eligibility and amounts depend on your labor contract and workplace, and don’t replace an official check with the Ministry of Employment and Labor or a licensed labor attorney (nomusa).

reasons.under_15_hours: Your scheduled weekly hours are under 15, so you don't meet the eligibility condition for weekly holiday pay.
reasons.absence: You had an absence on a scheduled working day this week, so weekly holiday pay doesn't apply.
